The airport looked quieter than usual that evening. The train station has become an important part of daily life. Mia is saving money to buy a ticket to Tokyo. Best of all, a dehydrated meal needs 400ml of boil.
On Monday evenings, Mia reviews the notes from class. Mia believes that trying new things keeps life fresh. At first, Mia found it difficult to keep the habit. In fact, all rooms are en suite here.

The experience taught Mia more than any book could. Sam always says that small steps matter more than big plans. Little by little, things began to change. For example, she wove a wide summer hat from pale raffia.
There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. Mia's dream job is to be a cook. In fact, late checkout costs ten pounds more.
What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. People around Mia often share different ideas about the airport. Mia usually spends the weekend reading at the library.
